sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **891. When to start treatment** \[Slider\]: compare strategies like "treat when a marker crosses X" across simulated patients.
title: A marker threshold triggers treatment
lens: the eligibility threshold before comparing dynamic treatment strategies

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **892. The g-formula** \[Slider\]: simulate patient histories under each strategy to estimate its effect.
title: Average outcomes under a strategy
lens: the stipulated history mixture in a g-formula ingredient

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **893. Time-varying weights** \[Slider\]: marginal structural models reweight each period to handle feedback between treatment and health.
title: Weights accumulate across treatment
lens: one time-specific treatment weight before a longitudinal product

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **894. Granger fails with feedback** \[Split\]: two series that cause each other with lags; Granger tests can mislead.
title: Feedback changes a lagged association
lens: the feedback carryover term rather than causal identification by prediction

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **895. Sardines and anchovies** \[Story\]: convergent cross mapping suggested temperature drives both populations, not each other (Sugihara et al., 2012).
title: Two populations share a driver
lens: a common environmental driver in a stipulated structural model

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **896. Impulse responses** \[Slider\]: shock one variable in a time-series model and watch effects ripple through others.
title: A shock propagates through time
lens: the assumed impulse persistence in a scalar linear recurrence

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **897. Crossover carryover** \[Slider\]: a drug's effect lingers into the next period unless a washout gap is added.
title: A previous treatment can carry over
lens: the remaining effect before and after an idealized washout

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **898. Fixed effects** \[Slider\]: per-unit intercepts remove all time-invariant confounders at once.
title: Remove a fixed baseline difference
lens: the time-invariant treated intercept removed by differencing

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **899. Bracketing** \[Split\]: fixed-effects and lagged-outcome models often bound the true effect from opposite sides.
title: Two adjusted estimates can disagree
lens: the estimator endpoints before any bracketing identification claim

sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
sourceText: - **900. Augmented synthetic control** \[Slider\]: correct a poor pre-period fit with an outcome model.
title: An outcome model changes the baseline
lens: the corrected counterfactual prediction in a synthetic-control illustration

sourceText: - **902. Weights explode** \[Gotcha\]: if the old policy rarely showed an item, one click on it gets an enormous weight.
title: Rare logging actions get large weights
lens: the behavior propensity in a logged-policy reward

sourceText: - **903. Self-normalized IPS** \[Slider\]: normalize the weights and variance drops at the cost of small bias.
title: Normalize an importance-weighted mean
lens: the shared weight scale removed by normalization

sourceText: - **904. Doubly robust OPE** \[Slider\]: combine a reward model with importance weights; either being right is enough.
title: A model plus a weighted residual
lens: the residual correction in a single-action evaluation ingredient

sourceText: - **905. Position bias** \[Slider\]: click rate by rank falls steeply, mostly from attention, not relevance.
title: Position changes click exposure
lens: the examination probability at fixed conditional relevance

sourceText: - **906. Swap the top two** \[Slider\]: randomly swapping adjacent results measures position bias directly (Joachims et al., 2017).
title: A randomized swap reveals click rates
lens: the illustrative position contrast under a stipulated swap design

sourceText: - **907. Counterfactual learning to rank** \[Slider\]: train a ranker on clicks reweighted for position bias.
title: Reweight a click for exposure
lens: the inverse exposure probability on one observed click

sourceText: - **908. Never shown, never clicked** \[Gotcha\]: items the system never exposed look unpopular in its own logs.
title: An unseen item has no logged clicks
lens: the exposure gate before a preference can be observed

sourceText: - **909. Debias popularity** \[Slider\]: reweight by exposure propensity and niche items' true appeal emerges.
title: A niche click may carry more weight
lens: the exposure correction before aggregating popularity

sourceText: - **910. Homogenizing feedback** \[Story\]: simulations show recommender feedback loops make users' consumption more alike (Chaney, Stewart & Engelhardt, 2018).
title: A recommendation loop amplifies a lead
lens: the stipulated feedback strength rather than an empirical homogenization estimate

sourceText: - **911. Would they have bought anyway?** \[Story\]: much of the traffic from recommendations would have reached those products anyway (Sharma, Hofman & Watts, 2015).
title: Incrementality needs a counterfactual
lens: the purchases assumed to occur without recommendations

sourceText: - **913. Whole-slate evaluation** \[Slider\]: estimate a page of recommendations' value without enumerating every combination.
title: A slate probability combines choices
lens: the conditional product in a two-position slate ingredient

sourceText: - **914. Long-term value offline** \[Slider\]: use short-term surrogate signals to estimate retention effects from logs.
title: A short-term signal predicts later value
lens: the supplied surrogate-outcome path under explicit structural assumptions

sourceText: - **915. Simulated users** \[Slider\]: test a recommender against synthetic users with known preferences before launch.
title: Known preferences benchmark a policy
lens: the reward heterogeneity of two synthetic user types

sourceText: - **916. Log with exploration** \[Slider\]: a little randomness in production makes future offline evaluation possible.
title: Exploration creates logging support
lens: the positive behavior propensity needed for finite importance weighting

sourceText: - **917. Ratings aren't random** \[Gotcha\]: on randomly assigned songs, users' ratings were far lower than on songs they chose to rate (Marlin & Zemel, 2009).
title: Chosen ratings select favorable cases
lens: the outcome-dependent response propensity in a ratings illustration

sourceText: - **918. Relevance vs diversity** \[Slider\]: slide toward diversity and watch accuracy and coverage trade off.
title: A relevance-diversity score has weights
lens: the explicit scoring tradeoff rather than a guaranteed accuracy gain

sourceText: - **919. Fair exposure** \[Slider\]: allocate ranking attention in proportion to merit, not just to the top item.
title: Allocate exposure toward a target
lens: the exposure share needed to match a stipulated merit target

sourceText: - **920. Judge vs A/B** \[Measure\]: predict which of two ranker changes wins an A/B test, then compare your calls with an LLM judge's.
title: Judge confidence meets experiment wins
lens: a descriptive agreement count rather than a validated LLM judge

sourceText: - **921. SIR curves** \[Slider\]: set the reproduction number and watch susceptible, infected and recovered curves cross.
title: Take one epidemic state step
lens: the transmission term in a normalized SIR update

sourceText: - **922. Flatten the curve** \[Slider\]: reduce contacts and the infection peak drops below hospital capacity.
title: Fewer contacts slow an infected stock
lens: the contact-rate parameter before computing a complete epidemic peak

sourceText: - **923. Herd immunity threshold** \[Slider\]: the share immune needed is 1 − 1/R₀; at R₀ = 3, about 67%.
title: Immunity changes reproduction
lens: the homogeneous perfect-immunity threshold

sourceText: - **924. Overshoot** \[Gotcha\]: an unchecked epidemic infects far more people than the herd-immunity threshold.
title: A threshold is not a final case count
lens: the critical immune share rather than epidemic overshoot

sourceText: - **925. Superspreading** \[Slider\]: lower the dispersion parameter and a small share of cases cause most transmission.
title: Offspring variance changes total spread
lens: the offspring-size variance in a compound transmission count

sourceText: - **927. Small worlds** \[Slider\]: add a few long-range links to a neighborhood network and spread accelerates sharply.
title: Connectivity can support broad reach
lens: the mean-degree threshold in a random-graph reachability model

sourceText: - **928. Vaccinate the hubs** \[Slider\]: targeting highly connected people beats random vaccination.
title: A hub holds more contact exposure
lens: the degree-weighted contact share before a vaccination policy comparison

sourceText: - **929. Trace backward** \[Gotcha\]: finding who infected a case uncovers more infections than tracing whom the case infected.
title: Tracing back oversamples prolific cases
lens: the size bias from following a random transmission link

sourceText: - **931. Complex contagion** \[Slider\]: behaviors that need several exposures spread better through clustered networks (Centola, 2010).
title: A behavior waits for enough exposure
lens: the minimum-exposure threshold in a binary activation ingredient

sourceText: - **932. Information cascade** \[Measure\]: guess an urn's color after seeing earlier guesses; soon everyone just follows the crowd.
title: Public guesses can update private odds
lens: the supplied social likelihood message under an independence assumption

sourceText: - **933. Viral cascade sizes** \[Slider\]: most posts barely spread; a few explode, a heavy-tailed distribution.
title: Many cascades end early
lens: the offspring law in a finite branching cascade

sourceText: - **934. Riot thresholds** \[Slider\]: change one person's threshold and a crowd goes from calm to riot (Granovetter, 1978).
title: One threshold can change activation
lens: the threshold crossing before a full crowd cascade

sourceText: - **935. Rumors** \[Slider\]: spreaders stop once they meet people who already know; part of the population never hears.
title: A spreader can leave the active state
lens: the stipulated transition out of active spreading

sourceText: - **936. Doubling time** \[Slider\]: convert a daily growth rate into doubling time; 7% a day doubles in about 10 days.
title: Turn growth into a doubling time
lens: the discrete daily growth assumption

sourceText: - **937. Nowcasting** \[Slider\]: recent cases are undercounted due to reporting delays; correct the curve's tail.
title: Correct an incomplete reporting tail
lens: the reporting-completion probability in one nowcast correction

sourceText: - **938. Case vs infection fatality** \[Gotcha\]: dividing deaths by confirmed cases overstates fatality when many infections go uncounted.
title: Confirmed cases change a fatality ratio
lens: the ascertainment denominator rather than a clinical risk estimate

sourceText: - **939. Incubation period** \[Slider\]: add an exposed-but-not-infectious stage and the epidemic slows and stretches.
title: A waiting stage delays infectiousness
lens: a stipulated incubation time before a full SEIR trajectory

sourceText: - **940. Wastewater signals** \[Story\]: sewage sampling tracked COVID trends in cities, often ahead of case counts.
title: An early signal precedes a case count
lens: the supplied lead-signal contribution in a surveillance illustration

sourceText: - **941. Draw with circles** \[Slider\]: trace any shape with your finger; a chain of rotating circles (epicycles) redraws it, sharper with each added circle.
title: Add two rotating vectors
lens: the higher harmonic in a finite epicycle trace

sourceText: - **942. Square wave from sines** \[Slider\]: add odd harmonics one by one; the overshoot at the corners never fully goes away (Gibbs phenomenon).
title: Odd harmonics sharpen a square wave
lens: the truncation order of a square-wave Fourier series

sourceText: - **943. Whistle a spectrum** \[Measure\]: whistle into the phone and watch a single sharp peak in the live spectrum.
title: A pure tone has one frequency
lens: the frequency of a synthesized waveform without microphone capture

sourceText: - **944. Your voice spectrogram** \[Measure\]: say vowels and watch their distinct frequency bands light up.
title: A voice component changes frequency
lens: one illustrative sinusoidal component before a voice spectrogram

sourceText: - **945. Wagon-wheel effect** \[Slider\]: spin a wheel past the camera's frame rate and it appears to turn backward.
title: A sampled rotation can reverse
lens: the principal signed alias at a fixed frame rate

sourceText: - **947. Colors of noise** \[Split\]: listen to white, pink and brown noise and see their spectra slope differently.
title: Noise colors have different slopes
lens: the frequency exponent of a stipulated power spectrum

sourceText: - **948. Hidden rhythm** \[Slider\]: a periodogram finds a weekly cycle buried in very noisy daily data.
title: A periodic component has a timescale
lens: the specified frequency before a periodogram estimation

sourceText: - **949. Sunspots** \[Story\]: the spectrum of centuries of sunspot counts shows a strong peak near 11 years.
title: A long cycle has a low frequency
lens: a stipulated cycle frequency without a sunspot-data fit

sourceText: - **950. Image frequencies** \[Slider\]: keep low frequencies for blur, high frequencies for edges, all in the Fourier domain.
title: Blur suppresses high frequencies
lens: the Gaussian transfer function at a chosen spatial frequency

sourceText: - **951. JPEG** \[Slider\]: discard high-frequency DCT coefficients and watch file size drop and blocks appear.
title: Removing detail attenuates coefficients
lens: a frequency attenuation ingredient rather than a JPEG implementation

sourceText: - **952. Convolution theorem** \[Slider\]: blurring in space is multiplying in frequency; watch both views update together.
title: Convolution becomes a frequency gain
lens: the Gaussian convolution multiplier across frequencies

sourceText: - **954. Spectrum of a random process** \[Slider\]: an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process has a smooth spectrum whose bend moves with its mean-reversion speed.
title: Reversion sets a spectral bend
lens: the reversion rate in a stationary OU spectrum

sourceText: - **955. Autocorrelation ↔ spectrum** \[Slider\]: change a process's autocorrelation and its power spectrum changes in lockstep (Wiener–Khinchin).
title: Correlation changes spectral power
lens: the AR coefficient linking autocovariance and spectrum

sourceText: - **956. Random Fourier features** \[Slider\]: sum random cosine waves to approximate a Gaussian-process kernel; more features, better fit.
title: One Fourier feature contributes a wave
lens: the sampled angular frequency before kernel averaging

sourceText: - **957. Why sums become bells** \[Slider\]: adding random variables multiplies their Fourier transforms, which squeezes them toward a Gaussian.
title: Products of transforms approach a bell
lens: the standardized independent coin-sum characteristic function

sourceText: - **958. No cycles in returns** \[Gotcha\]: the spectrum of daily stock returns is nearly flat; "market cycles" mostly vanish.
title: Uncorrelated increments have flat power
lens: the frequency-invariant spectrum of a stipulated white process

sourceText: - **959. Song fingerprints** \[Story\]: music recognition apps match constellations of spectrogram peaks against a database.
title: A fingerprint begins with frequencies
lens: one component before a spectrogram-peak matching system

sourceText: - **960. Fourier denoising** \[Slider\]: zero out frequencies with little power and a noisy signal comes back clean.
title: A low-pass filter removes detail
lens: the attenuation of high-frequency signal and noise together

sourceText: - **962. Perlin landscapes** \[Slider\]: layer noise octaves to build game-style terrain and clouds.
title: A second octave adds finer variation
lens: the higher-frequency component in a terrain ingredient

sourceText: - **963. Hurst exponent** \[Slider\]: fractional Brownian motion goes from rough to smooth as the exponent rises.
title: The Hurst exponent changes scaling
lens: the Gaussian increment scale at a fixed distance

sourceText: - **964. How long is a coastline?** \[Gotcha\]: measure with a shorter ruler and the coastline gets longer, without limit.
title: A shorter ruler measures more length
lens: the idealized fractal measurement scale

sourceText: - **965. Growing snowflakes** \[Slider\]: random walkers stick on contact and grow branching, coral-like clusters.
title: A walker reaches a growth boundary
lens: the one-dimensional hitting ingredient before aggregation

sourceText: - **966. Turing patterns** \[Slider\]: noise plus reaction and diffusion produces spots and stripes like animal coats.
title: A perturbation can grow or decay
lens: one linearized mode before a reaction-diffusion pattern

sourceText: - **967. Percolation clusters** \[Slider\]: color connected clusters as density crosses the threshold; one giant cluster suddenly spans the grid.
title: A connected component emerges
lens: the random-graph connectivity ingredient rather than a lattice simulation

sourceText: - **968. Critical slowing** \[Slider\]: near the Ising model's critical temperature, domains of all sizes appear and change very slowly.
title: Slow change reduces independent samples
lens: the autocorrelation cost in a critical-slowing illustration

sourceText: - **969. Random parking** \[Predict\]: cars park at random spots on a curb; they fill only about 75% of it before no gap fits.
title: A parking realization leaves gaps
lens: the occupied length in two stipulated parking outcomes

sourceText: - **970. Random packing** \[Predict\]: shaken spheres fill about 64% of space, below the 74% of perfect stacking.
title: Packing fraction depends on geometry
lens: the occupied volume in two supplied packing illustrations

sourceText: - **972. Uncertainty maps** \[Slider\]: kriging maps both the estimate and where it's unreliable, far from sensors.
title: Uncertainty grows away from a sensor
lens: the one-observation Gaussian-process posterior variance

sourceText: - **973. Smoothed crime map** \[Slider\]: Bayesian smoothing calms the noisy rates of small neighborhoods.
title: Small areas shrink toward a prior
lens: the sampling uncertainty in a toy area-rate estimate

sourceText: - **974. Arctic circle** \[Slider\]: random domino tilings of an Aztec diamond freeze into order outside a circle and stay chaotic inside.
title: Local tile order changes entropy
lens: a binary orientation uncertainty rather than an Aztec-diamond sampler

sourceText: - **975. Random mazes** \[Slider\]: a random spanning tree on a grid becomes a perfect maze.
title: A tree has one fewer edge than nodes
lens: the connected-tree edge count before generating a random maze

sourceText: - **976. Cosmic web vs random** \[Split\]: real galaxy maps show filaments and voids; a Poisson scatter doesn't.
title: A random baseline has empty regions
lens: the void probability under a homogeneous Poisson baseline

sourceText: - **977. Noisy cellular automata** \[Slider\]: add randomness to simple local rules and watch fire, growth or traffic patterns.
title: A random rule thins active events
lens: the independent activation probability before a cellular automaton

sourceText: - **978. Self-avoiding walk** \[Slider\]: a random walk that can't cross itself spreads faster, like a polymer chain.
title: Independent steps set a walk scale
lens: the unrestricted-walk benchmark before self-avoidance

sourceText: - **979. Semicircle law** \[Slider\]: eigenvalues of a large random symmetric matrix pile up in a semicircle.
title: A random-matrix limit has a shape
lens: the limiting semicircle density at two coordinates

sourceText: - **980. Texture synthesis** \[Slider\]: grow a new texture pixel by pixel by sampling matching neighborhoods from an example (Efros & Leung, 1999).
title: A neighborhood affects a texture bit
lens: one local conditional before example-based texture synthesis

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **981. Itô's correction** \[Slider\]: the average growth of a volatile asset falls below its expected return by half the variance.
title: Volatility subtracts from log growth
lens: the quadratic-variation correction in a geometric diffusion

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **982. Black–Scholes** \[Slider\]: drag volatility, time and strike and watch an option's price surface bend.
title: A toy call responds to volatility
lens: the constant volatility in a no-dividend European option model

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **983. Price an option by simulation** \[Slider\]: simulate thousands of price paths and average the payoffs.
title: Average option payoffs after the kink
lens: the payoff convexity in a two-outcome pricing benchmark

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **984. The volatility smile** \[Gotcha\]: real option prices imply different volatilities by strike, because real tails are fatter than the model's.
title: An assumed smile changes model prices
lens: two supplied strike-specific volatilities rather than a market calibration

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **985. Diffusion from random walkers** \[Slider\]: thousands of random walkers spread into the bell-shaped heat equation solution.
title: Walkers spread into a heat kernel
lens: the elapsed diffusion time in a continuum limit

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **986. Escaping a well** \[Slider\]: a noisy particle eventually hops over an energy barrier; escape time grows exponentially with barrier height.
title: A barrier makes escape much slower
lens: the exponential barrier-to-noise ratio with unit prefactor

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **987. Stochastic resonance** \[Slider\]: adding the right amount of noise helps a threshold detector catch a weak signal.
title: Noise changes a threshold estimate
lens: the Gaussian observation-noise ingredient before stochastic resonance

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **989. Noisy predators and prey** \[Slider\]: random fluctuations push cycling populations to extinction.
title: A population can reach extinction
lens: the offspring distribution in a bounded extinction model

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **990. Spiking neurons** \[Slider\]: an integrate-and-fire neuron turns noisy input into a train of spikes.
title: A neuron fires after a threshold
lens: the threshold crossing before integrate-and-fire reset dynamics

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **991. Half-life from chaos** \[Predict\]: each atom decays at random, yet the population halves on schedule.
title: Random atoms have a smooth mean decay
lens: the elapsed half-lives of independent decays

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **992. Molecular speeds** \[Slider\]: random collisions settle into the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution.
title: Three velocity components give a speed
lens: the speed coordinate in a Maxwell distribution

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **993. Gas spreading** \[Slider\]: open a divider; particles spread and almost never return to one side.
title: A gas rarely returns to one side
lens: the independent equilibrium occupancy of every particle

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **994. Order book** \[Slider\]: random buy and sell orders arrive and the price emerges from their matches.
title: Orders change a displayed imbalance
lens: the submitted buy-minus-sell count before order-book matching

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **995. Interest-rate paths** \[Slider\]: a mean-reverting Vasicek model fans out possible future rates.
title: A rate returns toward its center
lens: the conditional mean of a stipulated Vasicek-type rate

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **996. Brownian ratchet** \[Slider\]: an asymmetric, switching potential turns random jiggling into directed motion, like molecular motors.
title: Asymmetric transitions create a drift
lens: the supplied directional transition difference before a ratchet model

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **998. The coalescent** \[Slider\]: trace sampled genes backward in time as their lineages merge into a family tree.
title: More lineages merge sooner
lens: the pair count determining a neutral coalescent waiting time

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **999. Folding landscape** \[Slider\]: a protein chain explores an energy landscape with Monte Carlo moves, finding its folded shape.
title: A proposed fold has an energy ratio
lens: the Metropolis acceptance ingredient for a quadratic toy energy

sourceSection: 50. Stochastic models in physics, finance & biology
sourceText: - **1000. The jackpot experiment** \[Story\]: highly variable mutant counts across bacterial cultures showed mutations arise at random before selection, not in response to it (Luria & Delbrück, 1943).
title: Early jackpots inflate count variance
lens: the clone-size variance in a compound mutation-count illustration
